conviction_note: The Q4 revenue bar is fixed by the company's own guide and consensus sits on its midpoint, so there is no revenue edge. The FY27 guide is the line this stock has sold off on (-13.7% on the FY26 initial guide, -10.5% on the May cut, both from the confirmed-print 6-Ks), and I found nothing that says which way it goes. What is left is two small negatives. One is a likely year-end goodwill impairment, which is inferred and non-cash on a stock already at about 0.5x book. The other is shipping costs that rose after the May guide was set, which is a macro proxy the company had already named. They sum to -0.5 and I emit -0.3, because both caveats reach the number.
bar: Q4 FY26 revenue $51.27m consensus (MarketBeat/Cerbat Gem preview, https://www.thecerbatgem.com/2026/09/15/sangoma-technologies-sang-projected-to-release-quarterly-earnings-on-wednesday.html). This matches the company guide: FY26 $204-205m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1753368/000175336826000007/pressreleasef26q3.htm) less 9M revenue of $153.3m (Q1 $50.8m, Q2 $51.5m, Q3 $51.0m) implies Q4 $50.7-51.7m, midpoint $51.2m. Implied Q4 adj EBITDA is $6.5-8.7m (FY 15-16% margin less 9M $24.1m). FY27 consensus revenue was about $210.7m after the May print (Simply Wall St via Yahoo, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/sangoma-technologies-corporation-tse-stc-184556169.html), from one aggregator, so the guidance-line bar is soft.
positioning_check: US line: 20,600 shares short, 0.08% of float, 2.8 days to cover on about 7.9k ADV (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/SANG/short-interest, current page, undated). The sweep separately found an older alert of about 0.3% and 21 days (MarketBeat, 2026-01-13), which is stale. The primary line is TSX (STC), where CIRO's register cannot be reached. findings.finding: The June 30 2026 annual goodwill test is likely to produce an impairment. At FY25 the single CGU had only $34.2m of headroom on a $254.2m carrying value, and the company disclosed that a 10% change in the exit EV/revenue multiple moves fair value by about $22m. FY26 EBITDA guidance has since been cut from 17-19% to 15-16%, and equity of $248.4m at 2026-03-31 compares with a market cap near US$118m. Yet the Q3 interim statements say 'has not identified any indicators of impairment'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior impairment: FY25 recognised none, per the 40-F statements. No history on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: The previews carry EPS of -$0.07, which is ordinary amortisation-driven losses, with no charge in them. If an impairment were expected, the consensus net loss would be large. The equity market already values the company at about half of book, though, so the charge is information about book value that the multiple has mostly absorbed. That is why this is sized as a fraction.
findings.independence: The Q3 FY26 interim statements are a different document, and they carry the 'no indicators' language and $248.4m of equity: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001753368/000175336826000007/financialstatementsf26q3.htm. There is weak circumstantial support from the timing. The release lands on 2026-09-28, the 90-day NI 51-102 deadline after the June 30 year end, against Sept 17 and Sept 18 in the two prior years, and with an interim CFO since July 1 (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260604041373/en/Sangoma-Announces-CFO-Transition-Larry-Stock-to-Retire-June-30-Adrian-Back-Named-Interim-CFO-Board-Commences-Search-for-Permanent-Successor). The late date has other possible explanations, including the strategic review, so it is not sized on its own.

findings.finding: Freight costs kept rising after the May 13 guide. Asia to US West Coast spot rates were $3,624/FEU in late May, up 74% on late February, and the June Hormuz reopening broke down in early July. That bears on the product and fulfilment cost the company itself blamed for the margin cut, and it is a risk to the low end of Q4 EBITDA and to the first half of the FY27 margin guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance-line surprises on confirmed prints: -13.72% on 2025-09-17 (the FY26 initial guide below FY25 like-for-like) and -10.51% on 2026-05-13 (the margin cut). Both are US-line moves in a name trading about 7k shares a day there.
findings.why_not_priced: The company said in May that Hormuz and shipping costs were a headwind (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-sangoma-tech-reports-q3-2026-revenue-miss-93CH-4686877), so the direction is known. What may not be in consensus is the extra deterioration after the guide was set. It stays small because this is macro-to-company transmission: the incremental move has not been confirmed by the company or a counterparty. Hardware is also a minority of revenue, with Applications software and UCaaS at about 60% and MSP and Voice Infrastructure growing 9-17%, so the net effect is smaller still.
findings.independence: July status (reopening collapsed): https://www.mightyshipping.com/en/blog/2026-07-01-hormuz-reopening-july-freight-outlook. It is the same macro series, not company evidence.

searched_and_found_nothing: Strategic review outcome: no bidder name, halt, material-change report or rumour after 2026-05-13. The EDGAR submissions list shows no 6-K after 2026-06-04 (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001753368.json) and the company press-release page shows only the Jazzware partnership (08-25) and the date notice (09-22) (https://sangoma.com/company/press-releases/).
UCaaS sector take-privates in 2026 that might set a comp: none found.
Layoffs or WARN notices for Sangoma in 2026: none (results were Sangamo, a different company).

Insider trades: SEDI and CIRO are unreachable. The NCIB was renewed 2026-04-01 for up to 1.66m shares (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260401256957/en/Sangoma-Renews-Normal-Course-Issuer-Bid). This is known and in the price.
Permanent CFO appointment: none announced by 2026-09-28.
The large retail customer rollout (350+ sites, 15-20% deployed at Q3) sits inside the May guide, so it is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect and is not sized.
baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The two small negatives run with the -9.4% 20-day tape and a stock sitting near its 52-week low, so whatever they carry is probably already partly in the price. That is part of why the emitted -0.3 sits below the -0.5 sum.
lessons_applied: Impairment cut from -0.5 to -0.3 and kept as one_off. Lesson 2's reported-quarter exception covers a quantified impairment, and the 'what has worked' section covers a documented one. Mine is inferred from headroom arithmetic, which is the remeasurement-model reasoning the file says has not paid.

Shipping cut from -0.4 to -0.2. Lesson 5 treats the post-guide worsening as macro-to-company transmission with no company confirmation. Lesson 9 requires sizing net of the roughly 60% software and the growing infrastructure segments.

Rebuilt the base rate from the confirmed results 6-Ks (f25q4, f26q1, f26q2, f26q3: -13.72, +1.21, -1.45, -10.51) instead of the baseline's 8 rows, as the FPI lesson requires. The guidance line is the one that moves this name, and I have no edge on the FY27 guide, so the emitted move stays small.
The 'asking what was missed generates pessimism' lesson reached the number: both findings are negative and weak, so the emitted move is -0.3 against a -0.5 sum.
